You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.text:
**Figuring out memory tasks**

I need to save a global memory concept involving a template marker that interacts with noise and overlays copies of the template in various positions against a zeroed background. I should note that the background should have random values ranging from 0 to 7, with the marker color being one-ninth of the total forms of the template. My goal is to output a replacement for every zero cell that matches the translated pattern footprint. I also need to create a global memory for this task.

entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC overlay template on matching zero footprints', content='For ARC grids with a noisy two-color background (often 0 plus another color) and a small connected marker-colored shape, treat the marker shape as a binary footprint. Find every translation where all footprint coordinates land on background 0 (other cells in its bounding box are unrestricted); recolor the union of those footprint cells with the marker color. Keep grid dimensions and all other cells unchanged. Demonstrated twice: marker shapes colored 9 over random 0/3 or 0/6; solved a fresh 0/7 grid with marker 1. Important: match the footprint cells, not exact whole bounding-box contents; overlapping matches union naturally.', path='arc', global_=True)
print(entry)
